csv_agency: City of Chicago Dept of Planning & Development
csv_scope_of_work: The City of Chicago is seeking applications from qualified development teams to redevelop four Cityowned parcels located at 402 W. 111th St. and 11026 S. Eggleston Ave., in the Roseland community area. Consisting of 2.9 acres, the site presents a unique opportunity to create an equitable, transit-oriented project that leverages a future Chicago Transit Authority (CTA)Red Line Extension (RLE) station at 111th Street, and regional community anchors that include the Roseland Medical District, Fenger High School, Agape Community Center, and Pullman National Historical Park. The city expects proposals to include a variety of housing units for the site, including utilizing up to $5 million in Missing Middle Infill Housing grant funding.

title: Developer for 111th and Eggleston Development
short_description: Transit-oriented mixed-use housing development on four city-owned parcels in Chicago's Roseland area.
project_location: Chicago, Illinois, USA; 402 W. 111th St. and 11026 S. Eggleston Ave., Roseland community area.
project_scope: Redevelopment of four city-owned parcels totaling approximately 2.9 acres into an equitable transit-oriented development linked to a future CTA Red Line Extension station at 111th Street. The city expects a variety of housing units and integration with nearby community anchors including Roseland Medical District, Fenger High School, Agape Community Center, and Pullman National Historical Park. Up to $5 million in Missing Middle Infill Housing grant funding may be used.
services: Developer/design-build services and public transit planning for a transit-oriented redevelopment project.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a real estate development/developer solicitation rather than structural or engineering design.
- Focus is housing and transit-oriented development, with no defined bridge, long-span roof, stadium, or special structural scope.
- Public transit planning is mentioned, but no specific civil or structural engineering services are described.
- Could offer indirect strategic relevance due to transit-oriented urban development, but overall fit for sbp is low.
construction_cost_explanation: The source mentions up to $5 million in Missing Middle Infill Housing grant funding; this is not stated as total construction cost, but it is the only explicit monetary figure available.
fee_explanation: No planning or engineering fee is stated. The notice is for a developer/design-build team, so no realistic sbp fee can be derived from the provided information.
references_qualifications: Applications are sought from qualified development teams. No specific reference counts, technical qualifications, or engineering credential requirements are stated in the provided text.
contracting_authority: City of Chicago, Department of Planning & Development, Chicago, IL, USA. Contact: Jasmine Gunn. Phone: 312-744-4190. Email: jasmine.gunn@cityofchicago.org. Website: https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/sites/dpd-rfqs-and-rfps/home.html
notes: Target market is listed as transportation due to the future CTA Red Line Extension station, but the actual solicitation concerns redevelopment of a housing-led transit-oriented site. Questions deadline: 07/31/2026 05:00 PM CDT. Participation goals: MBE 26%, WBE 6%. Funding noted as grant.
